A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, algorithms, equations, Table 1, Figure 1, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 presents algorithms, theoretical regret bounds, computational arguments, and proofs. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper, including its appendices. The added geometric lemmas and computational construction do not report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The reduction and Algorithms 1–2 retain their main procedures. However, Section 4 replaces the ellipsoid-based implementation of Algorithm 1, line 6, with vertex decomposition and linear programming over active constraint normals. This changes a localized computational subroutine.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or conducts empirical evaluations. The combinatorial examples and settings with and without simulator access remain theoretical and unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the theoretical comparisons with Schneider and Zimmert, Neu and Valko, Dai et al., and both Liu et al. entries. No experimentally evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an experimental evaluation protocol. The doubling schedule, context-sample quantities, and simulator-call budget remain unchanged theoretical algorithm specifications.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, error analyses, or empirical case studies. Misspecification robustness is treated theoretically in both.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The concentration bounds and probability parameters in the retained theoretical analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains all regret and computational-complexity entries, and the advertised regret rates are unchanged. No empirical findings are added or revised. The comparator correction in Corollary 1 concerns its formal statement, assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 4 substantially revises the justification of polynomial-time normal-cone construction, replacing the fixed-margin feasibility argument with a finite LP construction. New Appendix B Lemmas 5–6 establish Minkowski-sum face decomposition and normal-cone intersection properties supporting it. Corollary 1 and its proof also change minimum to maximum regret over policies. The regret analyses in Appendices C–E otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same efficient reduction, combinatorial-bandit novelty claim, simulator-free regret rates, and simulator-assisted small-loss guarantee. The revised computational argument supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of misspecification, simulator benefits, limitations associated with exponentially many constraints, and three concluding open questions are retained. Appendix A's discussion of the discontinuity obstacle to discretization is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 now explicitly identifies the linear-optimization oracle required for efficient sampling. Section 4 documents the replacement subroutine's vertex-decomposition LP, active-constraint enumeration, and bounded-coefficient LP, providing more concrete implementation instructions than v1's ellipsoid-based outline.

R1.justification: V2 adds Weibel (2007) to support the new geometric lemmas and removes Grötschel, Lovász, and Schrijver (1988) with the replaced ellipsoid argument. The broader positioning against prior bandit research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4 gains three descriptive paragraph headings and revised explanations. V2 also makes limited grammatical edits, moves the definition of K earlier, adds funding acknowledgments, and updates Mayo's affiliation. The overall section and appendix sequence is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts NeurIPS title styling and narrower margins, reformats Table 1's header, and compacts Algorithm 2. The identical Figure 1 moves from page 5 to page 6. The same figure and comparison table remain, with no substantive redesign of their content.

improvement.justification: V1's Section 4 requires a fixed positive margin against every point of the polytope, an infeasible condition as written. V2 replaces this with explicit finite LPs supported by the new Appendix B lemmas, repairing an important gap in the polynomial-time implementation argument central to the paper's contribution. The oracle clarification and Corollary 1 correction improve precision further, although minimum-versus-maximum inconsistencies remain in Theorems 1 and 5.
